title: Decoupling Regime and Mechanistic Heterogeneity via Hierarchical Mixture-of-Experts for Global Carbon Flux Prediction
summary: A hierarchical mixture-of-experts model that separates environmental regimes from physical mechanisms for interpretable global ocean carbon-flux forecasting.
figure: Hierarchical regime and mechanism experts in REM-MoE.
detail: Level-1 routing represents geographical and seasonal regimes; Level-2 routing represents thermal, biological, and mixed processes. A global regime dictionary, affinity priors, and distinct latent channels help prevent expert collapse and entangled representations.
highlight: 38.4% lower 12-month MSE than PINP. 12 historical months predicting the next 12 months; target is monthly delta pCO2. Relative reduction = (0.1112 - 0.0685) / 0.1112. (Table 1, p. 6.)

title: StageNav: A Diagnostic Benchmark and State-Aligned RL Framework for Long-Horizon Navigation
summary: Geometrically verified task graphs and state-aligned reinforcement learning help navigation agents assess progress, recognize failure, and recover over long horizons.
figure: StageNav task-state verification and reinforcement-learning framework.
detail: StageNav-Bench parses long instructions into geometrically anchored DAGs and evaluates node-level execution and cognitive state alignment. The policy jointly predicts navigation actions and cognitive states (success, failure, or in progress).
highlight: 59.1% navigation success on R2R-CE. Unseen-validation continuous navigation; this is the paper's reported evaluation result. (Table II, p. 6.)

title: Carbon-ECS: A Benchmark and a Physics-Decoupled Model for the East China Sea Carbon Flux
summary: A 17-year, approximately 1 km benchmark and a physics-inspired model that pair large-scale transport modeling with iterative refinement of local carbon-flux detail.
figure: The TIDE-Net architecture combines global transport and local detail refinement.
detail: The dataset spans 2003–2019 (204 months) and repairs gaps through anomaly removal, wavelet denoising, and K-nearest-neighbor interpolation. The Frequency Global Module forecasts amplitude and phase; the Diffusion Local Refiner iteratively restores local detail.
highlight: 17 years of monthly data at approximately 1 km. Benchmark specification, not a comparative performance claim. (Table 1, p. 2.)

title: ForesightNav: Adaptive Semantic-Geometric Planning for Universal Zero-Shot Goal-Oriented Navigation
summary: A training-free navigation framework that combines semantic maps, graph-based target verification, and geometric frontier exploration for object, instance, and text goals.
detail: Context-aware semantic value maps guide broad search while online scene graphs verify fine-grained goal matches. Semantic score dispersion and graph-matching confidence choose among geometric exploration, semantic exploration, partial-match exploration, and target verification.
highlight: +18.6 percentage points in RoboTHOR success over UniGoal. RoboTHOR ObjectNav benchmark; percentage-point increase, not relative percent. (Table 1, p. 6.)

title: SHNet: A Lightweight Network Focusing on Shallow High-Resolution Features for PCB Defect Detection
summary: A lightweight PCB defect detector that preserves shallow high-resolution features through multi-scale adaptation, semantic alignment, and wavelet enhancement.
figure: SHNet architecture for detecting small defects on printed circuit boards.
detail: A YOLOv8s-based architecture removes the low-resolution detection head and retains deeper features as semantic guidance. MKAM provides scale-aware features; SSAM aligns shallow spatial detail and deeper semantics; WEM strengthens weak defect cues in the frequency domain.
highlight: 2.3 MB model with 0.97M parameters. Reported model artifact size and parameter count, consistent across the two evaluated PCB datasets. (Table 4, p. 8.)

title: Filter-Group Mixture-of-Experts Model for Remote Sensing Forged Target Perception
summary: Specialized edge, wavelet, texture, and directional filters form an expert ensemble that detects subtle forgery traces in remote-sensing imagery.
figure: Filter-group experts and multimodal gating in FG-MoE.
detail: A multimodal gating network routes visual and text features to specialized filter-based experts plus a standard expert. Tamper-mask reconstruction, visual question answering, and expert-balancing losses train the model jointly.
highlight: 92.95% overall accuracy on Real-RSCM. Remote-sensing forgery question answering on the Real-RSCM test set. (Table 1, p. 4.)

title: AnyTemplate: A Zero-shot Template Matching Approach for Arbitrary-Resolution and Scale-Agnostic Images
summary: A zero-shot template-matching framework that combines visual foundation models, aspect-ratio-preserving normalization, cross-attention, and geometric refinement across image scales.
detail: The geometry-aware normalization preserves aspect ratio and pads to the encoder canvas. A trainable cross-attention interaction module exchanges context between template and proposal features.
highlight: 94.1% accuracy on DEAMPB. Zero-shot template matching evaluation; use accuracy, not mAP, when citing Table II. (Table II, p. 5.)
